terms.comment: Any living creature, man included (animal … homō, Cic. Leg. 1.22), but as often the beasts as against man (Lewis & Short). An i-stem: ablative animālī, plural animālia, animālium.

evidence: Cic. Amic. 81: in bēstiīs, volucribus, nantibus, agrestibus, cicuribus, ferīs
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for every creature but man, tame or wild (Lewis & Short); also the wild beast of the arena. Its diminutive bēstiola is a little creature, a bug (Cic. ND 2.123).

evidence: Phaedr. 1 prol. 5–7: quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae
terms.comment: The wild animal, the talking beast of the fables; properly the feminine of ferus, wild.

terms.gloss: a beast, especially a large or fierce one; a monster
evidence: Cic. ND 1.97: elephantō bēluārum nūlla prūdentior (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: any living being; mostly an animal, as opposed to man (the gender varies, and is also neuter)
evidence: Cic. ND 2.22: animāns composque ratiōnis mundus est (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: alia animālia gradiendō, alia serpendō ad pāstum accēdunt, alia volandō, alia nandō
phrases.english: some animals come to their food walking, some crawling, some flying, some swimming
no animal sleeps more soundly (of the seal)

phrases.latin: Aperīs tū manum tuam, et implēs omne animal benedictiōne.
phrases.english: You open your hand and fill every living thing with blessing (the grace before meals).
Which animal did you like best?
no beast is wiser than the elephant

phrases.latin: ut requīrant atque appetant ad quās sē applicent ejusdem generis animantīs
phrases.english: so that they seek out and make for living creatures of their own kind to attach themselves to
In Aesop’s fables the animals talk.

phrases.latin: calumniārī sī quis autem voluerit, quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae, fictīs jocārī nōs meminerit fābulīs
phrases.english: and if anyone wants to carp because trees talk, not only animals, let him remember that we are playing in made-up stories

phrases.latin: loquī vērō arborēs, ferās cum hominibus gemere, verbīs certāre volucrēs, animālia rīdēre facimus
phrases.english: we make trees talk, beasts groan with men, birds dispute in words, and animals laugh
